Award Watch: lowercase aw, the second v of the w as a check

The a and the w are the typeface's own glyphs. The w's last up-stroke is carried on past x-height in its own direction, so the second v reads as a check; a hairline cut from the notch under the middle peak separates it from the first v, and in the two-tone version it takes the accent. All faces are under the SIL Open Font License. Each row: the plain aw for comparison, the one-colour cut version (the favicon form), then three accents.
